organism.overview: Amanita phalloides is a poisonous mushroom whose amatoxins can cause severe liver injury after ingestion. Toxicity is associated with consuming the mushroom, not with active venom delivery.
naturalHistory: It forms mycorrhizal associations with trees in temperate habitats.
Fruiting bodies can resemble edible mushroom species.
Amatoxin-containing tissues remain hazardous after cooking.

deliveryMechanism.summary: Poisoning follows ingestion of mushroom tissue containing amatoxins.
sequence: Mushroom tissue is collected or mistaken for an edible species.
Amatoxins are absorbed and reach susceptible organs.

habitats.name: Temperate woodland
habitats.summary: Commonly associated with temperate forests and trees with which it forms mycorrhizae.

ecologicalRoles.summary: The species participates in below-ground nutrient exchange with host trees.

externalProfile.sourceLabel: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention
summaryPoints: Mushroom poisoning is an ingestion hazard and should not be represented as venom delivery.
